advice.title: Prepare well, travel with peace of mind
advice.subtitle: From planning to your return: the key markers for a smooth trip to Burkina Faso.
advice.disclaimer: General information for guidance only. Always check official sources (Burkina Faso embassy, your country foreign ministry, WHO) before departure.

visa.title: Visa & passport
visa.text: Passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return date. Entry visa required for most nationalities: online e-visa or embassy visa. Keep a digital copy of your documents.

vaccines.title: Vaccines & preventive health
vaccines.text: Yellow fever vaccination is mandatory (international certificate checked on arrival). Antimalarial strongly recommended: see a travel clinic 4-6 weeks before departure. Update DTP, hepatitis A/B, typhoid.

season.title: When to go
season.text: Dry season November-February: the most pleasant weather, ideal for sightseeing. March-May: very hot (often over 40 C). June-October: rainy season, green landscapes but tracks can be tough.

money.title: Money & payments
money.text: Currency: CFA franc (XOF). Cash is king almost everywhere; cards work only in a few hotels and in Ouagadougou. Withdraw cash from ATMs in major cities and carry small notes.

security.title: Safety & itinerary
security.text: Check your foreign ministry travel advice before finalising your route; some regions are not advised. Prefer daytime travel, a local guide and identified accommodation. Register with your embassy if possible.

packing.title: What to pack
packing.text: Light, covering clothes, hat, sunglasses, high-factor sunscreen, insect repellent, first-aid kit (antimalarial, anti-diarrhoeal, rehydration salts), torch, adapter (type C/E plugs, 220V), filter water bottle.

health.title: Staying healthy
health.text: Drink only sealed bottled or filtered water. Avoid ice cubes, raw vegetables washed in tap water and lukewarm food. Wash hands often. Continue the antimalarial as prescribed, including after your return.

heat.title: Heat & sun
heat.text: Hydrate constantly, add a little salt to meals, rest during the hottest hours (12-3pm). Hat and sunscreen always. Watch for heatstroke signs (headache, nausea, confusion).

customs.title: Customs & etiquette
customs.text: Burkinabe hospitality (teranga) is warm: take time to greet people, it matters. Dress modestly, especially near places of worship. Use your right hand to give or receive. Always ask before photographing someone.

bargaining.title: Bargaining without stress
bargaining.text: Haggling is normal in markets and for taxis, never in fixed-price shops. Stay friendly, name a price, meet in the middle. Agree the taxi fare before getting in.

connectivity.title: Phone & internet
connectivity.text: Buy a local SIM (Orange, Moov) with your passport, at the airport or in a shop: cheap data and good city coverage. Hotel wifi is slow. Download offline maps.

language.title: Language
language.text: French is the official language and widely understood in towns. A few words of Moore (ne y windga: hello) or Dioula are always appreciated and open doors.

photos.title: Photos & respect
photos.text: Do not photograph official or military buildings or the airport. Ask permission for people; a small thank-you gesture is welcome. Some sacred sites forbid photography.

emergency.title: Useful numbers
emergency.text: Police: 17 - Fire/rescue: 18 - Ambulance: 112. Note your embassy and repatriation insurance numbers. Keep them offline and on paper.

healthWatch.title: Watch your health after returning
healthWatch.text: If you develop a fever within 3 months of returning, seek care quickly and mention your trip to Burkina Faso: malaria can appear late.
